bug_semantics: RequireScopes short-circuits with ctx.Next() whenever the JWT typ is session, before any scope or audience check. POST /login issues session tokens, so any authenticated non-admin satisfies JWTAuth/RequireAuth and then skips the only admin gate on routes that attach RequireScopes(admin:user|admin:settings) without a handler/service IsAdmin check. That lets a logged-in non-admin read GET /api/users (emails and admin flags), GET /api/system/logs, GET /api/system/visitor-stats, GET /api/system/check-update, and SSE /api/system/logs/stream. /ws/system/logs is registered on WSRouterGroup with no middleware; the handler only jwtUtil.ParseToken's the query token and never checks IsAdmin, scope, or audience, so the same session JWT tails live system logs.
flaw_origin: The session bypass was first written in reconstructable PR #195 member b47fa1c75d890cd080e3f6699bbfca8cd8d4b939, which created internal/middleware/scope.go with an explicit TokenTypeSession early-return and bound RequireScopes(ScopeAdminUser) onto GET /allusers as the only new admin control, while GetAllUsers still had no IsAdmin check. The Cursor plan for that PR stated session tokens should keep using existing role logic and access tokens should take scope checks; the implementation shipped the session pass-through without adding those role checks on the admin sinks. GitHub squash 3f8fb150158723aca31df2ae937a1aa7b31ac254 is the first-parent carrier onto main (absent in parent 45693330c7733364027e0aa07c102c4f01aab88a). Later 6df5673010720847e35d8bb8f60403e2cc4ab313 (v4.4.3) reused the same middleware on log routes, which cannot constrain session tokens.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-79665 / GHSA-q8hh-m6v5-4f3x is a live published record (CVE.org PUBLISHED; first-party GHSA-hmmq-qh6g-6wgh not withdrawn) for CWE-862. The attack is a logged-in non-admin presenting a normal session JWT. RequireScopes treats typ=session as full pass, so admin-scoped routes that never call IsAdmin authorize the caller. GetAllUsers at v4.5.0 returned every non-owner user's email; dashboard log/visitor-stats/check-update/SSE used the same pattern; /ws/system/logs never even entered that middleware. BIC search started from those cited lines, not from AI markers: git log -L/-S and --diff-filter=A on scope.go, then decomposition of squash #195. The smallest first-write is member b47fa1c7 (parent 1b280c25 verified present; scope.go/RequireScopes absent there). Squash 3f8fb150 is the main-line carrier, not the BIC. AI is judged only on that BIC commit object: Made-with: Cursor trailer plus human L1nSn0w author/committer, which is commit-object AI co-authorship of the first write of the session-skip mechanism and of attaching it to the admin GetAllUsers route. That is AI_ROOT_CAUSE, not NOT_AI. The v4.4.3 6df56730 change is an incomplete later remediation, not an introducer. Advisory patched boundary 4.5.1 matches 1b8c64d0 (GetAllUsers IsAdmin), which is the direct fix SHA; the session short-circuit itself was never removed, so log/WS/visitor-stats sinks stay open at HEAD, but the vendor's 4.5.1 security commit is a real, version-gated fix for the user-email path the advisory names.
